raw_response:
I've been farming these 8 mu for 30 years. I'm 58 now, never went to school, but I know this land better than anyone. My old man and me work it, and my daughter-in-law helps when she's not at the factory. We don't have much cash, so every jin of fertilizer and every hour of pumping water, I think hard about whether it's worth it.

I split the land into two pieces: 5 mu I do wheat then maize, back to back, same as most folks around here. The other 3 mu I plant cotton, because cotton money is steady and I know how to grow it.

**Wheat:** I already planted it last October, used the seeds I bought from the shop — better than saving my own, the shop seeds sprout stronger. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, same as always. Now it's spring, the wheat is turning green. I need to topdress soon, maybe half a bag of urea per mu at jointing stage. Pumping costs too much, so I'll irrigate three times: once when I put down the topdressing, once at heading if the sky doesn't give rain, and once at grain filling. Last year I got about 380 jin per mu. This year maybe 400 jin if the weather holds. I hire two young men for harvest, me and my old man can't cut and thresh like we used to.

**Maize:** After wheat comes out in early June, we got maybe five days to get the maize in the ground — sometimes less if rain comes. I'll buy hybrid maize seeds, about 3 jin per mu. I'll spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant, then see if the plants look yellow at the big trumpet stage — if they do, I'll topdress a little urea, maybe 5 kg per mu. Water is expensive, so I'll irrigate twice if it's dry, maybe only once if the summer rains are good. I expect around 450 jin per mu.

**Cotton:** Planting now, late April. I saved good cotton seeds from last year, no need to buy. For the 3 mu, I'll put down about three-quarters of a bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrows. Cotton doesn't need as much feeding as wheat. I'll irrigate twice — once after planting to help it settle, once in July if it's too hot and dry. The main worry is bugs, so I'll spray for aphids and the bollworm. Cotton picking is hard on my back, so I hire three days of help for that. I hope for around 220 jin of lint per mu.

**Tradeoffs:** Old Wang down the road cut his fertilizer last year and still did fine, so I thought about using less too. But then I remembered the year before last when I went light on the wheat and the yield dropped badly — lost more money than I saved. So this year I'm doing about the same as last year, not more, not less. My grandson needs school fees in the fall, so I can't spend everything on the fields. I have to keep some cash in my pocket. That's why I'm saving my own cotton seed and only hiring labor for the jobs I truly can't do myself.
